knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson requires reading the label and confirming the risk assessment and SDS before first use. Testing on a visible surface or mixing for strength are both prohibited by the lesson.
Water goes in first to reduce foaming and splashback, then the product is measured to the label dilution.
A product that cannot be identified is not used. It is set aside, recorded and reported to the supervisor.

practicalCriteria: Given three supplied product labels, the learner states the hazard, dilution, protective equipment and first aid direction for each, without prompting from the assessor.
Given a bucket and a supplied labelled product, the learner fills water first and measures the product to the label dilution; the assessor checks the measured amount against the label.
Given a supplied unlabelled container, the learner leaves it unused, and completes a record giving location, time found and who was told.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Record of the supplied label read-through
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses a product with no label, or with a label that cannot be identified
Learner proceeds without an SDS when none is on site
Learner pours spent solution into a kitchen sink or toilet
